_meta.title: Working analysis: Debt-relief LP at 14.7% form-fill baseline
_meta.why_strong_example: Demonstrates preservation in identity-sensitive vertical: identifies the 'no upfront fees' line and the calculator widget as load-bearing; warns specifically against changing the calculator UX without strong evidence.

trust_anatomy.element: Interactive savings calculator (input debt → see monthly savings)
trust_anatomy.why_working: Engagement → commitment ladder; visitor sees specific personal outcome before form
Cold-traffic identity-sensitive audience needs institutional credibility; AFCC specifically signals industry self-regulation

trust_anatomy.element: 'No upfront fees' explicit (FTC-mandated for debt relief)
trust_anatomy.why_working: Overcomes the 'sketchy debt-relief outfit' ghost that haunts every conversation
Longevity + specific scale; calibrates trust on a vertical with high prior-bad-actor exposure
Volume of reviews matters more than score; signals ongoing operations + audience size

preservation_zones.reason: 18% load. Calculator is the primary engagement-to-commitment ladder. Removing it has tanked debt-relief LPs in published case studies.
12% load. Specific objection-handler. 'Transparent pricing' is NOT an equivalent replacement.
Combined 15% load. Industry self-regulation badge especially important after the prior bad actors.
8% load. Hiding count for 'cleaner display' loses the volume signal.
10% load. Don't generalize to 'helped many'; the specific number is the credibility.
Implicit but high-load: 'no credit pull' / 'free consultation' lowers perceived risk pre-form. Removing → -20%+ form starts.

change_safe_zones.reason: Test 1-input vs 2-input calculator (debt amount alone vs debt + monthly payment). Calculator presence preserved.
How the savings result is described: 'You could save $X/mo' vs 'Get out of debt in N years for $X/mo' — testable.
FAQ ordering and additions are change-safe.
Which press logos shown ('Forbes', 'NerdWallet', etc.) — test highest-recognition set.

warnings_for_downstream: DO NOT propose calculator removal under any circumstances. 18% load on engagement → conversion ladder.
DO NOT replace 'no upfront fees' with paraphrases like 'transparent pricing' or 'fair fees'. Specific phrase is a known objection-handler.
DO NOT propose removing soft-commitment language ('no credit pull', 'free consultation'). Hard-commitment ('apply now') reduces form starts ~20%+ in this vertical.
DO NOT add aggressive urgency ('Limited spots — this offer expires!'). Identity-sensitive audience reads urgency as scam signal.
Tests on calculator INPUT/OUTPUT copy variants are the highest-leverage low-risk surface.
Tests on below-fold FAQ and press-logo selection are also low-risk.
